extraction.name: Introduction to the CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition
extraction.description: This paper describes the CoNLL-2003 shared task on language-independent named entity recognition. It provides background information on the English and German datasets, the evaluation method, an overview of participating systems, and a discussion of their performance.
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder
extraction.publisher: CNTS - Language Technology Group, University of Antwerp
extraction.citeAs: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder. 2003. Introduction to the CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition. In Proceedings of CoNLL-2003.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus, consisting of Reuters news stories. The German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, specifically extracted from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The English raw data was sourced from the Reuters Corpus. The German raw data was sourced from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, specifically from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: English data: Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997. Training and development sets from end of August 1996. Test set from December 1996. Preprocessed raw data covers September 1996. German data: Articles from one week at the end of August 1992 for training, development, and test sets. Raw data taken from September to December 1992.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For all data, a tokenizer, part-of-speech tagger, and a chunker were applied to the raw data. Language-specific tokenizers were created. The English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger. The German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger. Named entity tagging was done by hand. All data files contain one word per line with empty lines representing sentence boundaries. Each line contains four fields: the word, its part-of-speech tag, its chunk tag and its named entity tag. The IOB tagging scheme was used.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data was done by hand at the University of Antwerp. Mostly, MUC conventions were followed. An extra named entity category called MISC was added to denote all names not in the other categories (persons, organizations, locations). The IOB tagging scheme was used, where 'O' denotes outside an entity, 'I-XXX' for inside an entity of type XXX, and 'B-XXX' for the beginning of an entity when two entities of the same type are adjacent.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Named entities are assumed to be non-recursive and non-overlapping. When a named entity is embedded in another named entity, usually only the top-level entity has been annotated.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for developing and evaluating named-entity recognition systems, particularly those incorporating a machine learning component. It includes training, development (for parameter tuning), and test sets for English and German, as well as large files of unannotated data for exploring semi-supervised learning approaches.
